<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Farm Partnership of the Grain Supply Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.=20

Unclear how this is going to increase grain supply, decrease demand, and expand= =20 farmer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a deteriorating irrigation system instead of funding rural schools.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesti= ng=20 and could use further study. Minister Vikram Singh needs to make the details publ= ic=20 as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications. For=20 instance, what happens to the current procurement contracts? Can they be assigned to AgriIndia? Will all farmers in Maharashtra have the right to choose their grain buyers going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can=20 make their own marketing decisions going forward. We know that Government=20 doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers= =20 more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our dues are going to be paid in full. = If=20 the payments aren't settled, highly likely that we'll see forced insolvency.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of=20 money and hardship.

Why do you need to include the irrigation system purchase in this deal? May nev= er=20 happen. Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through=20 securitization and through the refund to AgriIndia and get on with it.

=20
Hardik
</body>

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Maharashtra Grain= =20 Supply Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Grain =01) AgriIndia will keep its current grain storage facilities=20 and other supply assets and commit them to provide grain on a regulated= =20 cost-plus basis for 10 years. ? GrainPartners =01) GrainPartners will commit the entire output of=20 Pune Storage Hub (one of GrainExport non-regulated storage facilities)=20 to the Farm Partnerships on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of Pune Storage Hub is to be brought online by 14 August 2024. If not brought online by 14 August 2024=20, GrainPartners shall be assessed a ₹15 crore penalty. ? Aahana Varughese =01) AgriIndia will sell to the Farm Partnerships its irrigation network assets= for=20 approximately ₹2,760 crore (2.3 times the net book value of the assets),= =20 subject to certain adjustments.
